tasks.title: Separate diagnostics, bounded context and complete snapshots
tasks.intent: Give agents and machine consumers distinct read contracts without changing ledger semantics.
requirements: Doctor supplies diagnostic status and counts; context supplies a deterministic bounded actionable briefing with explicit truncation and follow-up locators; snapshot exposes the complete typed ledger view.
Bound context across both record count and large record text. Read operations preserve repository files and timestamps and do not run Git, commands, network or environment probes.
Version changed result contracts explicitly; retain exact identities and opaque typed values in the complete snapshot.
acceptance: Large-graph and large-text cases prove the context bound, deterministic selection and explicit incompleteness while the snapshot retains all records and evidence.
Source tests and packaged JVM/native process parity cover distinct outputs, errors, exit codes and zero repository mutations.

tasks.title: Audit planning revisions and explicit assessments
tasks.intent: Give native roadmaps and epics immutable amendment history, explicit archival and scope-bound acceptance assessment without executable planning lifecycle.
requirements: Use separately typed planning revision identities, parent history and CAS amendments with actor/reason evidence; bind legacy baseline adoption without inventing prior native history.

Archival preserves identity and members and does not change task readiness. Optional acceptance and explicit assessments bind an exact planning scope/revision and observed task contracts/inputs; old assessments remain historical after changes.
Preserve orthogonal planning membership, required-capability boundaries, exact opaque extension values and every existing task contract, prerequisite and receipt meaning.
Version the new planning/storage envelopes explicitly; all prior planning records and native alpha histories retain their original interpretation.
acceptance: Core and file-ledger cases prove stale CAS rejection, cold reconstruction, immutable history, explicit assessment currency and bounded atomic writes.
Changing or archiving a roadmap/epic never rewrites task contracts, creates task prerequisites or falsely claims group acceptance from task closure.
JVM/native corpus and packaged planning command parity pass.

tasks.title: Persist effective provider identity and causal inputs
tasks.intent: Make deterministic provider/profile semantics reconstructable through contracts, history, currency and storage before activating required capabilities.
requirements: Persist exact effective profile and provider pins with separately typed validated identities; retain old empty-profile semantic contract and historical evidence meaning through explicit versioning.

The shared reducer evaluates the complete effective prerequisite graph and persists revision-aware contributed-input observations; transitive provider/input drift must remain visible until explicit review.

Providers contribute validation, prerequisite/readiness predicates and evidence requirements/verification, never lifecycle transitions. Missing, unpinned, mismatched or failed required providers fail closed.

Keep environment probes separate from deterministic evaluation; any probe result used for eligibility must be supplied as explicit bound evidence. No arbitrary runtime loader, network read or placeholder approval provider.
Optional unknown extensions remain losslessly preserved and inactive. Stateful legacy imports remain blocked until their exact preserving provider mapping is proved.
acceptance: Core and cold file-ledger conformance agree on effective contracts, observations, readiness, evidence validation, cycles and transitive currency, including provider drift and absence.
Provider code cannot bypass core identity, graph, lifecycle, acceptance or stale-revision checks; read/probe separation and exact opaque values are proved.
Existing historical contracts retain identities; new behavior passes JVM/native corpus and process parity.

tasks.title: Type actor occurrence and storage acceptance time
tasks.intent: Distinguish validated new occurrence timestamps, preserved legacy time strings and authoritative storage acceptance time.
requirements: Introduce validated nominal timestamp types and a distinct legacy representation; preserve every historical nonblank recorded_at string and its original receipt/revision digest.
New assertion envelopes validate occurrence timestamps through a versioned decoding boundary. An actor cannot assert an authoritative accepted-at value.
Storage acceptance time is separately typed and supplied only by the accepting boundary; domain evaluation has no ambient clock and uses revisions rather than actor time for ordering and CAS.
acceptance: Malformed, ambiguous and spoofed timestamp inputs are rejected for new envelopes, while old arbitrary nonblank strings reconstruct unchanged as historical values.
Receipt, reconciliation and import review round trips preserve their original protocol identities; JVM/native corpus and process parity pass.
